QuestionStmt.S: The co-ordinates of the point where the line joining the points $(2, -3, 1)$ and $(3, -4, -5)$ intersects the plane $2x + y + z = 7$ are

Solution.S:
The equation of the line passing through the points $(2, -3, 1)$ and $(3, -4, -5)$ is:

$$\frac{x - 2}{1} = \frac{y + 3}{-1} = \frac{z - 1}{-6} = t$$

$$\Rightarrow x = t + 2, \, y = -t - 3, \, z = -6t + 1$$

Substituting in $2x + y + z = 7$:

$$2(t+2) + (-t-3) + (-6t+1) = 7$$

$$2t + 4 - t - 3 - 6t + 1 = 7 \Rightarrow -5t + 2 = 7 \Rightarrow t = -1$$

$$x = 1, y = -2, z = 7$$

Thus the point is $(1, -2, 7)$, which corresponds to option D.
